text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
Brazil's state mining giant Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) was sold off to a group led by steelmaker CSN for 3.33 billion reais in the country's most controversial privatization to date.
-- JAPANESE TELL VOTORANTIM TO CEASE BIDDING FOR CVRD

"The Japanses were the first to tell me stop, stop, stop (bidding)," said Antnio Ermirio de Moraes, president of Votorantim Group, which was the only other bidder at the auction of state mining firm CVRD. Votorantim was grouped with Japanese and South African investors.
-- CVRD AUCTION SHOULD BRING $2 BLN INTO BRAZIL IN MAY

The sale of a controlling stake in CVRD should bring at least $2 billion into Brazil in May, helping to compensate for strong dollar outflows in recent months due to foreign debt payments, among other factors.

The duel between man and machine ended in a draw when chess champion Gary Kasparov and computer Deep Blue tied in the third match of a six game series. Kasparov won the first game and Deep Blue won the second.
-- CSN WOULD HAVE PAID MORE FOR CVRD

The CSN-led consortia which bought CVRD for 3.3 billion reais at an auction yesterday would have paid more for the state mining giant. "We were prepared to go a little further in the bidding," CSN President Benjamin Steinbruch said.

A $1.2 billion loan by Nations Bank to CSN, the largest loan ever to a private firm in South America, allowed CSN to lead the winning consortium in the 3.3 billion reais ($3.11 billion) purchase of CVRD.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
